matches.quote: In every state shown, higher T_c accompanies higher R_s and lower μ... develop at least a minimal quantitative model that reproduces the sign and magnitude of ΔR_s, Δn and Δμ
The Δ_L–ε correlation and the 35 K/95 K coincidences are weak, non-discriminating evidence... The Fig. 3e cartoon... is therefore a hypothesis, not a result.
plot T_c against μ, n, R_s and k_F·l for all prepared states: gate-swept, cycled, partially illuminated (L₁–L₄) and dark-relaxed
add an interface-sensitive polarization probe (low-T SHG, PFM through thin AlOₓ, Raman of the TO mode under gate) and an OV charge-state probe
The ~10 nA gate-current transient... plausibly integrates to ≳10¹³ cm⁻²... far more than the Hall Δn. Leakage through the substrate and contacts is not separated from displacement current.
All data appear to come from a single device, without controls... The authors should show the key effects in at least two or three independent devices
electrons escape over the edge of the confining potential into bulk or interfacial traps... this picture can account for the persistent R_s/μ changes without invoking PNRs.
The number of samples, the AlOₓ (Al) thickness... and dependence on reduction conditions... are not stated... including at least one with a different AlOₓ thickness
quantify the temperature rise during illumination... include a control in which the sample is heated in the dark to the LED-induced temperature.
Only ~10–15 points define the "linear" (95–35 K) and "steeper" (<35 K) regimes, with no fit statistics or error bars. Δ_L ≈ 0 near 95 K
changes in carrier distribution, confinement and disorder explain the data. OV charge-state changes alone, a well-established trap-charging picture, would explain both effects
develop at least a minimal quantitative model that reproduces the sign and magnitude of ΔR_s, Δn and Δμ, for example rate equations for trap/OV occupancy
add BKT analysis and perpendicular/parallel H_c2(T), from which the coherence length and any change in effective 2D thickness can be extracted.
compare the dielectric relaxation times τ = 1/ω(T) from Fig. 3c quantitatively with the transport kinetics, rather than relying on coincident temperatures.
None of the following is given: - retention time at base temperature; - endurance over many write/erase cycles; - cycle-to-cycle variance
The Arrhenius fits (Fig. 3c) span a narrow temperature window. No uncertainties are given for T_p, E_a or the attempt frequencies ω₁, ω₂
The manuscript never shows that illumination returns T_c, or R_s at the same temperature, to the pristine, pre-gating value... showing full R(T) curves.
measure the power, dose and wavelength dependence of erasure using several LEDs from near-IR to blue; include a control in which the sample is heated
The analysis also neglects the finite 2DEG sheet resistance (~800 Ω) and the wiring... present an equivalent-circuit or full impedance (Cole–Cole) analysis

notes: C5 (overdoping on the KTO dome) is judged partly raised by P13, which argues T_c tracks conventional 2DEG transport parameters (mobility/resistance/density) rather than PNR alignment and asks to plot T_c against n, mu, and R_s across all states. C2 (Arrhenius decay of the memory state across 10, 35, and 95 K) is judged partly raised by P18, P13, and P6, which ask for retention at base temperature, selective thermal erasure across the 35 K and 95 K thresholds, and quantitative comparison of transport relaxation times against the dielectric Arrhenius laws. C20 (large gate current at -50 V being leakage) is matched to P26, which notes that the ~10 nA current in Supp. Fig. 3a integrates to far more than Hall delta-n and is not separated from leakage.
